text: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) contains expressed nucleotide variation that may complement conventional expression analysis, yet its value for classifying local tissue states in peripheral artery disease (PAD) is uncertain. This study presents an exploratory machine-learning framework that converts quality-filtered scRNA-seq variants from 14 PAD samples (seven wound-exposed [WE] and seven unexposed wound-edge [UWE]) into sample-by-gene burden features. Reads were aligned, expressed variants were filtered at DP≥10, QUAL≥30, AD≥3, and VAF≥0.10, and gene burdens were normalized before comparison of linear support vector classification, logistic regression variants, and random forests using 5-fold stratified cross-validation repeated 30 times. The filtered cohort contained 133,025 variant records (84.83% SNPs and 15.17% INDELs). Linear SVC achieved the most stable leading performance (balanced accuracy 0.97±0.03; ROC-AUC 0.99). Feature filtering increased the variance represented by the first two principal components from 39.1% to 55.6% and separated WE from UWE samples descriptively. Positive WE-associated coefficients included VCAN, SPP1, POSTN, MMP9, and COL1A1, whereas KRT18, EPCAM, CLDN4, and MUC1 were UWE-associated. The results support mutation-derived gene burden as a promising hypothesis-generating representation, while requiring independent genomic validation and larger cohorts before clinical interpretation.

text: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is a systemic atherosclerotic disorder that limits limb perfusion and carries substantial risks of functional decline, tissue loss, and cardiovascular events. Its worldwide prevalence and risk-factor burden have made PAD a continuing public-health challenge [1]. Tissue behavior is spatially heterogeneous: cells at an exposed wound surface experience a microenvironment distinct from cells at an unexposed wound edge. Single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic studies of PAD muscle and related vascular injury states have begun to resolve this diversity, including sex-associated responses and cell-specific remodeling programs [2], [3].

text: Most scRNA-seq studies emphasize gene expression. However, aligned reads also contain expressed single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and short insertions/deletions (INDELs) [4]. Aggregating such observations by gene can reduce the dimensionality of sparse site-level calls and yield a mutation-derived gene-burden representation. This is biologically attractive because human plaque studies have identified heterogeneous immune, stromal, and smooth-muscle-cell states whose functions converge on inflammation and extracellular-matrix remodeling [5]-[7]. It is also technically difficult: an RNA-derived call is conditional on expression and read coverage and may reflect mapping ambiguity, RNA editing, or allelic imbalance rather than a confirmed genomic mutation [8].

text: Machine learning can integrate many weak gene-level signals, but limited cohorts create a high risk of optimistic performance. Interpretable models are therefore preferable to unrestricted complexity [9]. Recent engineering studies have illustrated both PAD prediction and gene-expression subtype classification with machine learning [10], [11]. Here, we extend that logic to expressed-variant burden. The study objective was to construct a leakage-aware framework, compare six classifier configurations, and identify signed biomarkers distinguishing WE from UWE samples. The work is exploratory and evaluates sample-state classification rather than patient-level diagnosis.

text: The analysis used scRNA-seq FASTQ files from 14 PAD samples divided evenly between WE and UWE states (Figure 1). The workflow followed standard scRNA-seq processing principles. Reads were aligned with STARsolo, which uses the STAR alignment framework. Expressed variants were called with BCFtools, mapped to genes using GENCODE annotation [12], and retained only when depth (DP), Phred-scaled quality (QUAL), alternate-allele depth (AD), and variant allele fraction (VAF) satisfied the thresholds shown in (1).

text: Variant calling from scRNA-seq is intrinsically sensitive to coverage, allelic dropout, and expression, as demonstrated by comparative benchmarks and single-cell variant callers [13], [14]. Consequently, all retained events are described as expressed variant records rather than validated germline or somatic mutations.

A log transform and training-derived standardization produced (3), with ε preventing division by zero. Genes whose training-fold variance fell below τ were excluded according to (4).

text: PCA projected standardized burdens onto directions maximizing covariance as in (5). Logistic regression estimated the class probability in (6). Linear support vector classification (SVC) minimized the regularized hinge-loss objective in (7), and random forest probability was averaged across T trees as in (8). Implementations followed scikit-learn [15]; the model families correspond to support-vector machines [16], L1/L2-regularized linear models [17], and random forests [18], while the PCA formulation follows [19].

text: Six configurations were compared: Linear SVC; logistic regression with L2 or L1 regularization; logistic regression after retaining 10 principal components; logistic regression after KBest selection; and a 500-tree random forest. Evaluation used 5-fold stratified cross-validation repeated 30 times.

text: Hyperparameters and data-dependent transformations were selected within the training partition by inner cross-validation, so the held-out fold did not influence scaling, filtering, selection, or tuning. This nested structure addresses selection bias [20], although repeated resampling cannot replace external validation in a small dataset [21]. Balanced accuracy in (9) was the primary metric. Precision P, recall R, F1-score, and ROC-AUC were secondary measures; (10) defines the three threshold-based quantities. Precision-recall behavior remains important whenever future cohorts are imbalanced [22].

text: Across 14 samples, 133,025 records passed quality filtering: 112,841 SNPs (84.83%) and 20,184 INDELs (15.17%). The mean total yield was 9,501.8±1,511.6 records per sample (median 10,185; range 7,165–11,785). SNP counts averaged 8,060.1±1,473.0, whereas INDEL counts averaged 1,441.7±223.8. In every sample, the reported total equaled SNPs plus INDELs, providing an internal consistency check (Fig. 3).

text: Linear SVC, L2 logistic regression, and PCA10 logistic regression each achieved a mean balanced accuracy of 0.97. Linear SVC had the smallest reported dispersion (±0.03 versus ±0.04) and was therefore selected as the most stable leading model. All three reached precision, recall, and F1-score of 0.97 and ROC-AUC of 0.99. KBest logistic regression was lower (balanced accuracy 0.89±0.19; ROC-AUC 0.94), followed by random forest (0.85±0.22; 0.91) and L1 logistic regression (0.84±0.21; 0.90). Because fold-level predictions were unavailable, these differences were not assigned formal statistical significance (Fig. 4).

text: Before filtering, PC1 and PC2 explained 25.3% and 13.8% of variance, respectively (39.1% combined), with partial proximity of WE and UWE samples near the origin. In the selected-feature representation, the same 14 samples separated along PC1; PC1 and PC2 explained 36.7% and 18.9% (55.6% combined). This projection is descriptive because feature selection and visualization used the analyzed cohort rather than an external test set (Fig. 5).

text: This study shows that expressed-variant records can be transformed into a compact gene-burden matrix that supports accurate WE-versus-UWE classification under repeated, stratified resampling. The strongest result is not merely the high mean score, but the agreement among three linear configurations and the lower dispersion of Linear SVC. The weaker and more variable random forest is consistent with the instability expected when a flexible model is fitted to far more candidate features than samples. Likewise, the reduced performance of L1 and KBest configurations suggests that aggressive sparse selection may discard distributed signal.

text: The biological direction of the model is coherent with vascular remodeling. WE-associated VCAN, POSTN, COL1A1, FN1, MMP9, and TIMP1 collectively implicate extracellular-matrix deposition, turnover, adhesion, and repair, while SPP1 and IL1B point to inflammatory activation. Single-cell plaque studies have independently described smooth-muscle and stromal transitions linked to extracellular matrix [5], [6], and calcified plaques show cell-state complexity relevant to these processes [23]. SPP1-positive macrophages have also been connected with vascular fibrosis [24]. Conversely, UWE-associated epithelial and junctional genes – including KRT18, EPCAM, CLDN4, OCLN, and MUC1 –suggest relative preservation of barrier-like programs. These parallels support biological plausibility, but they do not prove that the observed RNA variants causally regulate expression or PAD.

provenance: supplied manuscript text; not independently reproduced
text: A mutation-derived gene-burden representation of 14 PAD scRNA-seq samples separated WE from UWE states with strong repeated-cross-validation performance. Linear SVC was the most stable leading classifier, and its signed markers emphasized matrix remodeling and inflammation in WE samples versus epithelial and barrier-associated features in UWE samples. These findings establish a reproducible hypothesis-generating framework, not a clinical diagnostic model. Matched DNA confirmation, donor-aware external validation, and cell-type-resolved analysis are necessary before the reported biomarkers can support mechanistic or translational conclusions.
